messages:
nora: quick design question  ordering of CTAs on the quickstart card. current order is [Try sample] then [Create API key]. some PMs worry that users click sample and never wire up credentials. thoughts?

diego: we saw this before  if sample runs in a sandbox you can let users try immediately but nudge them with a persistent toast: 'Connect API key to save work'. that keeps the friction low but surfaces the next step.

oliver: a11y nit: any toast or persistent nudge must be reachable by keyboard and have clear aria-live semantics. avoid assertive announcements for non-critical nudges. also current primary CTA color on the card is ~#3b82f6 which is borderline at 14px. bump contrast or font-weight.

sam: microcopy: change CTA "Try sample" -> "Run sample (no key)" and secondary CTA "Create API key" -> "Add API key" to reduce ambiguity. keeping the sandbox phrasing helps set expectation.

marta: telemetry point: differentiate sandbox runs vs real runs. add keys: onboarding.sample.run_sandbox, onboarding.sample.run_real, onboarding.api.add_key. we'll A/B test variants where the API key CTA is more prominent (primary) vs secondary.

nora: UX question: should we show both CTAs side-by-side or stack primary above secondary on mobile? stacking may push important content down.
diego: stack on mobile, side-by-side on desktop. use responsive breakpoint at 720px. keep spacing tight.

oliver: keyboard focus flow: tab order should go primary CTA -> secondary CTA -> learn-more link. when the user triggers "Run sample (no key)" open the sample drawer and move focus into the drawer's primary run button. Esc should close and return focus to the CTA. ensure close button is first tabbable element.

sam: implementation tiny snippet for responsive layout:

```css
.quickstart-ctas { display: flex; gap: 8px; }
@media (max-width: 720px) { .quickstart-ctas { flex-direction: column; } }
```

oliver: motion/accessibility: respect prefers-reduced-motion for the drawer open animation and avoid focus shift that confuses screen reader users. when you announce state changes, keep messages short like "Sample ready to run".

marta: experiment plan: control = current layout; variant A = sandbox CTA labeled explicitly + persistent toast; variant B = promote API key CTA to primary. primary metric: conversion to first saved project within 24h. secondary: percent who add API key within 7 days. guardrail: increased help requests.

nora: decision so far: update microcopy per sam, increase CTA contrast per oliver, show both CTAs but responsive stack on mobile, add persistent but dismissible toast after sandbox run, and add telemetry keys. diego/tariq can you prototype the toast and drawer behaviour?
diego: yep will prototype. one note  toast should have a "Save my work" CTA that takes user to key flow, and a "Dismiss" that fires onboarding.toast.dismiss. keep it non-modal.

oliver: final a11y checklist from me: 1) CTA contrast >=4.5:1 or 16px/semibold; 2) keyboard order + focus ring visible 3px; 3) drawer focus management + close first; 4) toasts aria-live polite and reachable by keyboard; 5) icons get aria-labels. i'll sign off after dev prototype.

sam: i'll update figma copy and color tokens and upload frames by Thu AM. tagging oliver for final check. :thumbsup:

marta: i'll add experiment config to tracking doc and share telemetry keys with eng.

deploy-bot: reminder: onboarding design freeze Fri 5pm PT. please link comps to RELEASE ticket.

nora: thanks everyone  leaving thread open for any last UX or a11y nits.
